title: Aadhaar Biometric Authentication Mandatory for Subsidised LPG Refills From October 1
excerpt: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas says 27.43 crore consumers - 89.9% of the total - have already completed authentication; the rest must do so to keep booking subsidised refills, or opt out and pay market price.
body:
• From October 1, 2026, domestic LPG consumers must complete Biometric Aadhaar Authentication to keep booking refills at the subsidised regulated price; the rule was announced by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas on September 19.
  • As of September 19, 27.43 crore consumers — 89.9% of the total — had already completed authentication and need take no further action.
  • Those who do not authenticate must explicitly opt out via OMC digital channels and will receive LPG at market price, in 5 kg or 10 kg cylinders; authentication can be done at delivery, at showrooms, or via the IndianOil ONE, HelloBPCL and HP PAY apps.

The deadline is now firm. From October 1, 2026, subsidised LPG refills will require Biometric Aadhaar Authentication (BAA) — any domestic consumer who has not linked their connection to Aadhaar biometrics will not be able to book cylinders at the regulated price with subsidy. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas confirmed the enforcement date on September 19, ending months of rolling extensions.

The scale of the exercise is already nearly complete: 27.43 crore active consumers, or 89.9% of the total, had finished authentication by September 19 and need do nothing further — their refills continue as before. The remaining roughly one in ten consumers is the target of the final push.

How to comply — and what non-compliance means

Authentication can be completed in three ways: during refill delivery, at the distributor's showroom, or from home through the three oil marketing companies' mobile apps — IndianOil ONE for Indane, HelloBPCL for Bharatgas, and HP PAY for HP Gas.

Consumers who cannot or will not complete BAA are not cut off entirely, but they must register that choice on OMC digital channels — consumer portals, mobile apps, WhatsApp chatbots or IVRS — and will then receive LPG at market price without subsidy, restricted to 5 kg or 10 kg cylinders subject to local availability.

"Linking each connection to the Aadhaar-authenticated consumer helps prevent diversion of subsidised domestic cylinders for commercial and industrial use, removes duplicate and ineligible connections, and makes subsidy delivery transparent and targeted."

— Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, statement quoted in The Hindu BusinessLine

Why the government is doing this

The rationale is fiscal and enforcement-driven. India has more than 32.70 crore domestic LPG consumers, including over 10.50 crore PM Ujjwala Yojana beneficiaries — the deepest subsidy tier. In Delhi, a PMUY beneficiary paid ₹642 for a 14.2 kg cylinder in June 2026 against a market price above ₹1,600; general consumers paid ₹942. With that kind of price gap, diversion of subsidised domestic cylinders to commercial and industrial users has been a chronic enforcement problem, and the biometric linkage is designed to deduplicate connections and verify that the subsidy reaches genuine households.

The deadline itself has a history: the original cutoff was June 30, extended several times before a final September 14 deadline for completing authentication. October 1 is when the rule starts biting.

What NRIs should do

This one lands directly on diaspora households. Many NRIs maintain or fund LPG connections for elderly parents in India — and the registered consumer is the one who must authenticate. If your parents' connection is among the unauthenticated 10%, make sure the BAA is completed via the delivery agent, the showroom or the OMC app before October 1, or the household will have to opt out and pay full market price. It is also a policy signal worth noting: India's subsidy architecture is moving decisively toward biometric-verified targeting.
